measured: The exposure is rebuilt in Europa's frame from its own event list: the good time, the drift, the tracking residual, the events placed, Europa's radius on the grid, and the darkest-bin statistics in the claimed sector.

The statistics are reported in two normalisations, because a control annulus away from Europa does not give a scatter of one: the formal Poisson significance, and the same bin divided by the scatter the limb annulus itself shows.
The same latitude band on the northern side is measured as well, so a claim that is really about Europa's south pole can be told from one the whole limb shows.
notVerified: This stage does not build the Jovian background model of Sparks et al. (2016) section 3.1, which is accumulated from one-second slices in Jupiter's own rest frame with Europa's path masked out and divided by a matching exposure-time image. A polynomial surface fitted outside 1.6 Europa radii stands in for it, and Jupiter's belts survive that fit.

This stage does not build the Europa model of Sparks et al. (2016) section 3.2: the USGS 500 m Galileo mosaic projected onto a sphere, contrast adjusted by a fitted factor, multiplied by an Oren-Nayar illumination function of fitted roughness and convolved with a composite TinyTim point-spread function that mixes a far-ultraviolet model with a 300 nm one for the red leak. The azimuthal average of the data stands in for it, and it does not carry Europa's albedo pattern.
The detector's geometric distortion is not corrected: the events are counted at the coordinates the file stores. The archive applies that correction only when it rectifies an image.

Because neither model is reproduced, no number here is a reproduction of the significance Sparks et al. report. What is comparable is the location of the darkest bin and the scatter the statistics actually show.
